# Dependency Upgrade Fix: k8s.io/api 0.26.5 → 0.27.2

## Context

You are working on the **elastic/cloud-on-k8s** Go project. The dependency **`k8s.io/api`** has been upgraded from version **0.26.5** to **0.27.2** in the project's manifest/lock files. This upgrade introduces breaking changes that cause test failures.

**You must perform the dependency upgrade yourself, end-to-end.** Update the project's manifest and lock files to apply the dependency bump described above, then adapt the source code so the upgraded project's test suite passes against the new dependency version.

## Working Directory

The project source code is located at `/app`. 

## Constraints

- **Do not modify any test files.** The test suite is the evaluation oracle and will be re-applied verbatim before grading.
- Restrict your changes to the project's source code so that the existing tests pass against the upgraded dependency.

17. package internal
18. 
19. import (
20. 	"fmt"
21. 
22. 	"k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache"
23. 	"k8s.io/client-go/util/workqueue"
24. 	"sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime/pkg/client"
25. 	"sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime/pkg/event"
26. 	"sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime/pkg/handler"

28. 
29. 	"sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime/pkg/predicate"
30. )
31. 
32. var log = logf.RuntimeLog.WithName("source").WithName("EventHandler")
33. 
34. var _ cache.ResourceEventHandler = EventHandler{}
35. 
36. // EventHandler adapts a handler.EventHandler interface to a cache.ResourceEventHandler interface.
37. type EventHandler struct {
38. 	EventHandler handler.EventHandler
39. 	Queue        workqueue.RateLimitingInterface
40. 	Predicates   []predicate.Predicate
41. }
42. 
43. // OnAdd creates CreateEvent and calls Create on EventHandler.
44. func (e EventHandler) OnAdd(obj interface{}) {
45. 	c := event.CreateEvent{}
46. 
47. 	// Pull Object out of the object
48. 	if o, ok := obj.(client.Object); ok {
49. 		c.Object = o
50. 	} else {
51. 		log.Error(nil, "OnAdd missing Object",
52. 			"object", obj, "type", fmt.Sprintf("%T", obj))
53. 		return
54. 	}
55. 
56. 	for _, p := range e.Predicates {
57. 		if !p.Create(c) {
58. 			return
59. 		}
60. 	}
61. 
62. 	// Invoke create handler
63. 	e.EventHandler.Create(c, e.Queue)
64. }
65. 
66. // OnUpdate creates UpdateEvent and calls Update on EventHandler.
67. func (e EventHandler) OnUpdate(oldObj, newObj interface{}) {
68. 	u := event.UpdateEvent{}
69. 
70. 	if o, ok := oldObj.(client.Object); ok {
71. 		u.ObjectOld = o
72. 	} else {
73. 		log.Error(nil, "OnUpdate missing ObjectOld",
74. 			"object", oldObj, "type", fmt.Sprintf("%T", oldObj))
75. 		return
76. 	}
77. 
78. 	// Pull Object out of the object
79. 	if o, ok := newObj.(client.Object); ok {
80. 		u.ObjectNew = o
81. 	} else {
82. 		log.Error(nil, "OnUpdate missing ObjectNew",
83. 			"object", newObj, "type", fmt.Sprintf("%T", newObj))
84. 		return
85. 	}
86. 
87. 	for _, p := range e.Predicates {
88. 		if !p.Update(u) {
89. 			return
90. 		}
91. 	}
92. 
93. 	// Invoke update handler
94. 	e.EventHandler.Update(u, e.Queue)
95. }
96. 
97. // OnDelete creates DeleteEvent and calls Delete on EventHandler.
98. func (e EventHandler) OnDelete(obj interface{}) {
99. 	d := event.DeleteEvent{}
100. 
101. 	// Deal with tombstone events by pulling the object out.  Tombstone events wrap the object in a
102. 	// DeleteFinalStateUnknown struct, so the object needs to be pulled out.
103. 	// Copied from sample-controller
104. 	// This should never happen if we aren't missing events, which we have concluded that we are not
105. 	// and made decisions off of this belief.  Maybe this shouldn't be here?
106. 	var ok bool
107. 	if _, ok = obj.(client.Object); !ok {
108. 		// If the object doesn't have Metadata, assume it is a tombstone object of type DeletedFinalStateUnknown
109. 		tombstone, ok := obj.(cache.DeletedFinalStateUnknown)
110. 		if !ok {
111. 			log.Error(nil, "Error decoding objects.  Expected cache.DeletedFinalStateUnknown",
112. 				"type", fmt.Sprintf("%T", obj),
113. 				"object", obj)
114. 			return
115. 		}
116. 
117. 		// Set obj to the tombstone obj
118. 		obj = tombstone.Obj
119. 	}
120. 
121. 	// Pull Object out of the object
122. 	if o, ok := obj.(client.Object); ok {
123. 		d.Object = o
124. 	} else {
125. 		log.Error(nil, "OnDelete missing Object",
126. 			"object", obj, "type", fmt.Sprintf("%T", obj))
127. 		return
128. 	}
129. 
130. 	for _, p := range e.Predicates {
131. 		if !p.Delete(d) {
132. 			return
133. 		}
134. 	}
135. 
136. 	// Invoke delete handler
137. 	e.EventHandler.Delete(d, e.Queue)
138. }

17. package internal
18. 
19. import (
20. 	"fmt"
21. 
22. 	"k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache"
23. 	"k8s.io/client-go/util/workqueue"
24. 	"sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime/pkg/client"
25. 	"sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime/pkg/event"
26. 	"sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime/pkg/handler"
27. 	logf "sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime/pkg/internal/log"
28. 
29. 	"sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime/pkg/predicate"
30. )
31. 
32. var log = logf.RuntimeLog.WithName("source").WithName("EventHandler")
33. 
34. var _ cache.ResourceEventHandler = EventHandler{}
35. 
36. // EventHandler adapts a handler.EventHandler interface to a cache.ResourceEventHandler interface.
37. type EventHandler struct {
38. 	EventHandler handler.EventHandler
39. 	Queue        workqueue.RateLimitingInterface
40. 	Predicates   []predicate.Predicate
41. }
42. 
43. // OnAdd creates CreateEvent and calls Create on EventHandler.
44. func (e EventHandler) OnAdd(obj interface{}) {
45. 	c := event.CreateEvent{}
46. 
47. 	// Pull Object out of the object
48. 	if o, ok := obj.(client.Object); ok {
49. 		c.Object = o
50. 	} else {
51. 		log.Error(nil, "OnAdd missing Object",
52. 			"object", obj, "type", fmt.Sprintf("%T", obj))
53. 		return
54. 	}
55. 
56. 	for _, p := range e.Predicates {
57. 		if !p.Create(c) {
58. 			return
59. 		}
60. 	}
61. 
62. 	// Invoke create handler
63. 	e.EventHandler.Create(c, e.Queue)
64. }
65. 
66. // OnUpdate creates UpdateEvent and calls Update on EventHandler.
67. func (e EventHandler) OnUpdate(oldObj, newObj interface{}) {
68. 	u := event.UpdateEvent{}
69. 
70. 	if o, ok := oldObj.(client.Object); ok {
71. 		u.ObjectOld = o
72. 	} else {
73. 		log.Error(nil, "OnUpdate missing ObjectOld",
74. 			"object", oldObj, "type", fmt.Sprintf("%T", oldObj))
75. 		return
76. 	}
77. 
78. 	// Pull Object out of the object
79. 	if o, ok := newObj.(client.Object); ok {
80. 		u.ObjectNew = o
81. 	} else {
82. 		log.Error(nil, "OnUpdate missing ObjectNew",
83. 			"object", newObj, "type", fmt.Sprintf("%T", newObj))
84. 		return
85. 	}
86. 
87. 	for _, p := range e.Predicates {
88. 		if !p.Update(u) {
89. 			return
90. 		}
91. 	}
92. 
93. 	// Invoke update handler
94. 	e.EventHandler.Update(u, e.Queue)
95. }
96. 
97. // OnDelete creates DeleteEvent and calls Delete on EventHandler.
98. func (e EventHandler) OnDelete(obj interface{}) {
99. 	d := event.DeleteEvent{}
100. 
101. 	// Deal with tombstone events by pulling the object out.  Tombstone events wrap the object in a
102. 	// DeleteFinalStateUnknown struct, so the object needs to be pulled out.
103. 	// Copied from sample-controller
104. 	// This should never happen if we aren't missing events, which we have concluded that we are not
105. 	// and made decisions off of this belief.  Maybe this shouldn't be here?
106. 	var ok bool
107. 	if _, ok = obj.(client.Object); !ok {
108. 		// If the object doesn't have Metadata, assume it is a tombstone object of type DeletedFinalStateUnknown
109. 		tombstone, ok := obj.(cache.DeletedFinalStateUnknown)
110. 		if !ok {
111. 			log.Error(nil, "Error decoding objects.  Expected cache.DeletedFinalStateUnknown",
112. 				"type", fmt.Sprintf("%T", obj),
113. 				"object", obj)
114. 			return
115. 		}
116. 
117. 		// Set obj to the tombstone obj
118. 		obj = tombstone.Obj
119. 	}
120. 
121. 	// Pull Object out of the object
122. 	if o, ok := obj.(client.Object); ok {
123. 		d.Object = o
124. 	} else {
125. 		log.Error(nil, "OnDelete missing Object",
126. 			"object", obj, "type", fmt.Sprintf("%T", obj))
127. 		return
128. 	}
129. 
130. 	for _, p := range e.Predicates {
131. 		if !p.Delete(d) {
132. 			return
133. 		}
134. 	}
135. 
136. 	// Invoke delete handler
137. 	e.EventHandler.Delete(d, e.Queue)
138. }
